description: Physics matriculation 2021: topic → subtopic → concept/keywords index mapped to question ids and textbook pages. Used by the offline search tutor.

topics.title: Physical quantities, measurement and vectors
topics.concept: Fundamental and derived quantities, systems of units (SI/MKS, CGS), prefixes and conversions, measuring instruments, errors, scientific notation, significant figures, dimensions, scalars and vectors.

subtopics.title: Quantities, systems of units, prefixes and conversions
subtopics.concept: Fundamental quantities (length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount of substance, luminous intensity) and derived ones. MKS/SI: metre, kilogram, second; CGS: centimetre, gram, second. Prefixes: milli 10⁻³, micro 10⁻⁶, nano 10⁻⁹, kilo 10³, mega 10⁶.

subtopics.title: Measuring instruments, errors and significant figures
subtopics.concept: Vernier calliper: reading = main-scale reading + vernier-scale reading × least count (0.1 mm); micrometer screw gauge 0.01 mm. Scientific notation a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10. Rounding to a given number of decimal places or significant figures; accuracy vs precision.

textbook_refs.section: 1.1.2 Systems of measurement – measuring length with a vernier calliper

subtopics.title: Scalars and vectors
subtopics.concept: Vectors have magnitude and direction; two vectors are equal only if they have the same magnitude and the same direction. Collinear vectors add algebraically; perpendicular ones by Pythagoras; resolution Ax = A cos θ, Ay = A sin θ. Displacement is a vector.

textbook_refs.section: 1.3.2 Position and displacement vectors – equality of vectors

topics.title: Motion in one dimension
topics.concept: Distance and displacement, speed and velocity, acceleration, equations of uniformly accelerated motion, free fall and graphs of motion.

subtopics.title: Distance, displacement, speed and velocity
subtopics.concept: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time (rest periods included in the time); average velocity = displacement ÷ time. Displacement = straight-line change of position with direction.

subtopics.title: Acceleration and the equations of uniformly accelerated motion
subtopics.concept: a = (v − u)/t; v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ½(u + v)t.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1.4 Acceleration; 2.1.6 Equations of uniformly accelerated motion

subtopics.title: Freely falling objects
subtopics.concept: Without air resistance all bodies fall with the same acceleration g (≈ 10 m/s²) whatever their mass; objects thrown upward decelerate at g, stop at the top and fall back.

subtopics.title: Graphs of motion
subtopics.concept: Distance–time graph: slope = speed. Velocity–time graph: slope = acceleration, area = displacement. Uniform velocity → horizontal straight v–t line; uniform acceleration → sloping straight line; a vertically thrown body has a straight v–t line crossing the time axis at the top.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.2 Velocity-time graph for motion with uniform velocity
2.1.4 Acceleration; 2.1.6 Equations of uniformly accelerated motion

topics.title: Force and motion
topics.concept: Force and its effects, Newton's laws, universal gravitation, normal force, friction, momentum, impulse and collisions.

subtopics.title: Force, its effects and the net force
subtopics.concept: A force can change the shape, size, speed or direction of motion of a body – not its mass. Forces along one line add algebraically (take one direction as positive).

textbook_refs.section: 3.1.1 The concept of force – net force
3.1.1 The concept of force – effects of a force

subtopics.title: Newton's laws of motion
subtopics.concept: First law (inertia); second law F = ma; third law: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction (acting on different bodies).

subtopics.title: Newton's law of universal gravitation
subtopics.concept: F = Gm₁m₂/r², G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²; weight W = mg.

subtopics.title: Friction
subtopics.concept: Friction opposes relative motion; reduced by polishing, lubrication (oil, grease, graphite), ball bearings and rolling. Maximum static friction > kinetic (sliding) friction > rolling friction. μ = f/N; a larger μ means more friction.

textbook_refs.section: 3.2.3–3.2.5 Reducing friction, types of friction, laws of friction

subtopics.title: Momentum, impulse and collisions
subtopics.concept: p = mv; impulse F·Δt = Δp; momentum is conserved in collisions. Elastic collision: kinetic energy also conserved (equal masses, one at rest → they exchange velocities); inelastic: kinetic energy lost.

topics.title: Work, energy and power
topics.concept: Work done by a force, kinetic and potential energy, conservation of mechanical energy, power and efficiency of machines.

subtopics.title: Kinetic and potential energy; conservation of energy
subtopics.concept: KE = ½mv², PE = mgh. Without friction mechanical energy is conserved: v = √(2gΔh) for a drop Δh whatever the path.

textbook_refs.section: 4.2.4 Mechanical energy – conservation of mechanical energy

subtopics.title: Power, machines and efficiency
subtopics.concept: P = W/t = Fv (watt). Efficiency = work output ÷ work input × 100 %; always below 100 % in real machines.

topics.title: Motion in two dimensions and moments
topics.concept: Projectile motion, uniform circular motion, relative velocity, moments and the conditions of equilibrium.

subtopics.title: Projectile motion
subtopics.concept: Horizontal and vertical motions are independent. Launched at speed u and angle θ: maximum height H = u² sin²θ / 2g, time of flight 2u sin θ / g, range u² sin 2θ / g.

subtopics.title: Relative motion
subtopics.concept: Velocity of A relative to B: v(A rel. B) = v(A) − v(B) (vector difference). Bodies moving towards each other: relative speed = sum of speeds; same direction: difference.

textbook_refs.section: 1.3.1 Relative velocity in a fixed frame of reference

subtopics.title: Moments and equilibrium
subtopics.concept: Moment = F × perpendicular distance. First condition of equilibrium (translational): net force = 0; second condition (rotational, principle of moments): net moment = 0.

textbook_refs.section: 1.4 Moment of a force – conditions of equilibrium

topics.title: Temperature, heat and thermodynamics
topics.unit: Unit 2 – Temperature, Heat and the Laws of Thermodynamics
topics.concept: Temperature scales and thermometers, heat, specific heat capacity and latent heat, heat transfer and the laws of thermodynamics.

subtopics.title: Temperature, scales and thermometers
subtopics.concept: Liquid-in-glass thermometers use mercury or coloured alcohol; advantages: direct reading, simple and quick; disadvantages: unsuitable for very high and very low temperatures, reading depends on the exposed column. T(K) = t(°C) + 273.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 2 – Temperature, Heat and the Laws of Thermodynamics

subtopics.title: Heat, specific heat capacity and latent heat
subtopics.concept: Q = mcΔT (c in J/(kg·°C)); latent heat Q = mL.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 2 – Temperature, Heat and the Laws of Thermodynamics
textbook_refs.section: 2.1.4–2.1.5 Heat and its units; specific heat capacity

subtopics.title: Transfer of heat
subtopics.concept: Conduction (through solids, particle to particle, e.g. along a metal rod), convection (fluids, by movement of the fluid) and radiation (electromagnetic waves, no medium needed).

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 2 – Temperature, Heat and the Laws of Thermodynamics

subtopics.title: Laws of thermodynamics and thermodynamic processes
subtopics.concept: First law ΔU = Q − W. Isothermal (T constant), isobaric (P constant), isochoric/isometric (V constant, W = 0), adiabatic (Q = 0).

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 2 – Temperature, Heat and the Laws of Thermodynamics

topics.title: Electrostatics
topics.concept: Electric charge, conductors and insulators, charging, Coulomb's law, electric field, electric potential energy and potential.

subtopics.title: Electric charge, conductors and charging
subtopics.concept: Two kinds of charge, positive (carried by protons) and negative (carried by electrons); like charges repel, unlike attract; charge is conserved and quantised (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).

subtopics.title: Coulomb's law and the electric field
subtopics.concept: F = kq₁q₂/r², k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C². E = kq/r², pointing away from + and towards − charges; fields add as vectors. In electrostatic equilibrium the field inside a conductor is zero.

textbook_refs.section: 3.6 Electric field lines – field of a conductor
3.7 Electrical potential energy and electric potential

subtopics.title: Electric potential energy and potential
subtopics.concept: U = kq₁q₂/r (negative for unlike charges); V = kq/r (scalar – potentials of several charges simply add).

textbook_refs.section: 3.7 Electrical potential energy and electric potential

topics.title: Direct current circuits
topics.concept: EMF and potential difference, current, meters, resistance and Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits, electrical energy and power.

subtopics.title: Current, EMF and meters
subtopics.concept: I = Q/t (ampere). Ammeter (in series) measures current; voltmeter (in parallel) measures potential difference; ohmmeter – resistance; wattmeter – power.

subtopics.title: Ohm's law and resistors in series and parallel
subtopics.concept: V = IR. Series: R = R₁ + R₂ + …, same current; parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …, same voltage, currents divide inversely to resistance.

textbook_refs.section: 4.5.3 Resistors in series and in parallel

subtopics.title: Electrical energy and power
subtopics.concept: P = VI = I²R = V²/R; energy = Pt (J or kWh).

textbook_refs.section: 4.6 Electrical energy and power in circuits

topics.title: Reflection of light and mirrors
topics.unit: Unit 5 – Geometrical Optics Part I: Reflection of Light and Mirrors
topics.concept: Sources and propagation of light, pinhole camera, laws of reflection, plane and spherical mirrors, the mirror equation and magnification.

subtopics.title: Plane and spherical mirrors; mirror equation
subtopics.concept: 1/f = 1/dₒ + 1/dᵢ, f = R/2, m = −dᵢ/dₒ = hᵢ/hₒ (real is positive). Concave mirror, object beyond C: real, inverted, diminished image between F and C. Convex mirror: always virtual, erect, diminished.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – Geometrical Optics Part I: Reflection of Light and Mirrors
textbook_refs.section: 5.5.3 Formation of images by spherical mirrors

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – Geometrical Optics Part I: Reflection of Light and Mirrors
textbook_refs.section: 5.5.4 The mirror equation; 5.5.5 Sign convention for mirrors

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 5 – Geometrical Optics Part I: Reflection of Light and Mirrors
textbook_refs.section: 5.5.3 Formation of images by spherical mirrors

topics.title: Refraction of light, lenses and optical instruments
topics.unit: Unit 1 – Geometrical Optics Part II: Refraction of Light and Lenses
topics.concept: Laws of refraction, refractive index, real and apparent depth, total internal reflection, mirages, lenses, optical instruments, the eye, dispersion and colour.

subtopics.title: Refraction, refractive index, apparent depth, total internal reflection and mirages
subtopics.concept: n = c/v; relative index n₁₂ = n₂/n₁; Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂; apparent depth = real depth ÷ n. Mirage: light bends away from the normal in hotter, less dense air near the ground until total internal reflection occurs.

Unit 1 – Geometrical Optics Part II: Refraction of Light and Lenses

textbook_refs.section: 1.4 Dispersion of light – refraction through a prism (minimum deviation)

subtopics.title: Optical instruments and defects of vision
subtopics.concept: Myopia (short sight): image in front of the retina – corrected with a concave (diverging) lens; hypermetropia – convex lens. Microscope, telescope, camera, projector.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 1 – Geometrical Optics Part II: Refraction of Light and Lenses
textbook_refs.section: 1.3.6 The human eye and defects of vision

subtopics.title: Prisms, dispersion and colour
subtopics.concept: Minimum deviation: n = sin((A + Dm)/2) / sin(A/2). White light disperses into a spectrum; primary and secondary colours; filters.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 1 – Geometrical Optics Part II: Refraction of Light and Lenses
textbook_refs.section: 1.4 Dispersion of light – refraction through a prism (minimum deviation)

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 1 – Geometrical Optics Part II: Refraction of Light and Lenses

topics.title: Magnetism and electromagnetic induction
topics.concept: Magnets and magnetic fields, fields of currents, magnetic forces on conductors and moving charges, electromagnets, electromagnetic induction and transformers.

subtopics.title: Magnets, magnetic materials and magnetic fields
subtopics.concept: Permanent magnets keep their magnetism for a long time (hard magnetic materials, e.g. steel, alnico); temporary magnets (soft iron) lose it. The field direction is the direction of the force on a north pole – the way a compass needle points.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1.1 Magnets and their properties – magnetic field and compass
2.1.2 Types of magnet – permanent and temporary

subtopics.title: Magnetic field of currents (wire and solenoid)
subtopics.concept: Long straight wire B = μ₀I/(2πr); solenoid B = μ₀nI = μ₀NI/L, μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.3 Magnetic field around a current-carrying solenoid

subtopics.title: Magnetic force on conductors and moving charges
subtopics.concept: F = BIL sin θ; F = qvB sin θ. A charge moving perpendicular to B moves in a circle: r = mv/(qB), period T = 2πm/(qB) (independent of speed).

textbook_refs.section: 2.3.2 Force on a moving charge in a magnetic field

topics.title: Waves and sound
topics.concept: Wave motion and types, wave terms and speed, behaviour of waves, sound production, speed and audibility, intensity level, pitch and quality, electromagnetic waves.

subtopics.title: Wave motion, terms, speed and behaviour
subtopics.concept: All waves are produced by vibrations. Transverse and longitudinal waves; crest to adjacent trough = λ/2; v = fλ. Water waves travel faster in deeper water (speed depends on depth). Reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference.

textbook_refs.section: 3.1.3 Terminologies in waves; 3.1.4 Velocity of a wave

subtopics.title: Sound: production, speed and audible range
subtopics.concept: Sound needs a medium; v(air) ≈ 331 + 0.6t m/s (t in °C). Audible range 20 Hz–20 000 Hz; the ear is most sensitive between 1000 Hz and 5000 Hz.

subtopics.title: Intensity level, pitch and quality of sound
subtopics.concept: β = 10 log(I/I₀) dB, I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m²; every +10 dB multiplies the intensity by 10. Pitch depends on frequency, loudness on amplitude, quality on overtones.

subtopics.title: Electromagnetic waves
subtopics.concept: Oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, at the same frequency and in phase; speed c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum; the EM spectrum from radio to gamma rays.

topics.title: Fluid mechanics
topics.concept: Density and relative density, pressure in liquids and the atmosphere and its applications, Pascal's principle, buoyancy, Archimedes' principle and flotation.

subtopics.title: Pressure in liquids and gases; atmospheric pressure and its applications
subtopics.concept: P = F/A; liquid pressure P = hρg, the same in all directions at a given depth, acting perpendicular (normal) to any surface in contact. Atmospheric pressure works syringes, rubber suckers, drinking straws and siphons.

textbook_refs.section: 1.2.1 Pressure and its units; 1.2.2 Liquid pressure
1.2.1 Pressure and its units; 1.2.2 Liquid pressure
1.2.4 Applications of liquid and atmospheric pressure

subtopics.title: Pascal's principle and hydraulic machines
subtopics.concept: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every part of the fluid: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ (hydraulic jack, press, brakes).

textbook_refs.section: 1.3.1 Applications of Pascal's principle – hydraulic jack

subtopics.title: Buoyancy, Archimedes' principle and flotation
subtopics.concept: Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced. A floating body displaces its own weight: ρ(body) × h(body) = ρ(liquid) × h(submerged), so the submerged depth is inversely proportional to the liquid's density.

topics.title: Quantum physics
topics.concept: Models of the atom, the dual nature of light, photon energy and momentum, the photoelectric effect and its applications, atomic spectra and X-rays.

subtopics.title: Structure of the atom and atomic models
subtopics.concept: Thomson's plum-pudding model (positive charge with electrons spread uniformly through it); Rutherford's nuclear model (tiny dense positive nucleus); Bohr's model with energy levels.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The structure of the atom – atomic models

subtopics.title: Dual nature of light; photon energy and momentum
subtopics.concept: Interference and diffraction are explained by the wave theory; photoelectric effect by the particle (photon) theory. E = hf = hc/λ, p = hf/c = h/λ; photons are electrically neutral. Number of photons per second = power ÷ hf.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.2 Energy of a photon (energy and momentum)
2.2.2 Energy of a photon – properties of photons

subtopics.title: Photoelectric effect
subtopics.concept: hf = W₀ + KEmax; KEmax = ½mv²max = eV₀ (stopping potential); threshold frequency f₀ = W₀/h. UV light makes a negatively charged zinc plate lose its charge (electrons are emitted).

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.3 Photoelectric effect – stopping potential and work function
